basis: Developmental impairment and structurally abnormal hair define the syndrome; type 2 diabetes in 2/4 is separately diagnosed.
Pulmonary vascular hypertension; the underlying lung disease or hypoxia is a separate causal condition.
A disorder of iris pigmentation, confined to the ocular axis.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia with micromelia, abnormal ossification and cartilage stippling in 80-99%.
Hindbrain malformation involving the cerebellum and brainstem; associated hydrocephalus remains within the neurologic axis.
Complement-mediated renal thrombotic microangiopathy with hemolysis and thrombocytopenia; vascular injury with hypertension occurs in 30-79%.
Branched-chain amino acid metabolism defect; toxic encephalopathy and brain injury are common (>30%), especially in classic disease.
Isolated congenital structural malformation of the femur.
Mitochondrial encephalopathy; cardiomyopathy 8/15 and brittle hair 6/11. Respiratory failure is neuromuscular; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury.
Lipid-storage myopathy; cardiomyopathy and hepatic steatosis each occur in 30-79%. Mild intellectual disability reported in 2/3 is omitted at the cap.
Obstetric umbrella; no organ within the 13 axes is consistently affected across pregnancy disorders.
Oxidative phosphorylation defect; brain dysfunction and skeletal myopathy commonly affect >30%. Cardiac and renal damage vary substantially by subtype.
Inflammation of tendon sheaths in the foot and ankle; an immune-mediated mechanism is not established.
A peripheral nerve sheath neoplasm; cellular atypia does not establish another organ of origin.
Gram-negative bacterial infection of the meninges; additional organ injury is not consistently common across this group.
Congenital skeletal muscle disease; respiratory muscle weakness does not itself establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Haemophilus infection directly inflames the meninges; permanent hearing loss occurs in fewer than 30%.
Basal cell carcinoma arises from the cutaneous epithelium of the vulva, establishing a dermatologic origin.
Blepharophimosis affects the eyelids, and intellectual disability establishes neurodevelopmental involvement; both define the syndrome.
Extensive open spinal dysraphism involves the neural tube and failure of vertebral arch closure.
A neuroblastic tumor arising from the peripheral sympathetic nervous system, with ganglionic and Schwannian components.
Isolated male infertility caused by abnormal sperm acrosomes; reproductive function has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Skeletal dysplasia and hair/subcutaneous loss define the syndrome; FSGS and LV hypertrophy each affect 3/7. Possible hepatic injury (transaminases 3/7) omitted at cap.
An umbrella for breast lactation disorders; endocrine gland disease is not intrinsic to the group.
Multiple skeletal synostoses define the disease; hypermetropia affects 4/5 and ptosis 2/5. Hearing-loss annotations each report 1/5, insufficient to establish >=30%.
